The legend states that while imprisoned, Dandinus miraculously healed a blind man, who in turn revealed the location of a hidden Christian community to Roman soldiers. Dandinus and the community were executed for their faith.

Another reference to Dandinus is found in the 'De Virtutibus' (On Virtues) by the 13th-century Franciscan friar and theologian Bonaventure of Bagnoregio. In this work, Bonaventure mentions Dandinus as an example of Christian fortitude, recounting his story of being sentenced to death for refusing to sacrifice to idols during the persecutions under Emperor Decius in the 3rd century.
